title: Large Language Models in the Loop: A Stability- and Network-Aware Survey in Networked Control, Cyber-Physical, and Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: arXiv:2609.16599v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Modern networked control systems (NCSs), cyber-physical systems (CPSs), and complex multi-agent network systems (CNSs) increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) for high-level decision-making. However, the slow, stochastic nature of LLMs directly conflicts with the strict stability and safety guarantees required by these physical systems. This survey presents a unified analysis of how LLMs can be admitted into the control loop of NCS, CPS, and CNS without compromising closed-loop guarantees. We organize this around a core principle: the LLM operates as a slow supervisor adjusting high-level goals and constraints, while a fast, certified inner loop maintains physical stability. Under this framework, LLM integration maps directly to classical networked control challenges, where inference latency acts as delay, API failures as packet dropouts, tokenization as quantization, and hallucinations as bounded disturbances. translated_title: 环路中的大语言模型：面向网络化控制、信息物理与多智能体系统的稳定性与网络感知综述
translated_abstract: 现代网络化控制系统、信息物理系统和复杂多智能体网络系统日益依赖大语言模型（LLM）进行高层决策。然而，LLM缓慢且随机的特性与这些物理系统所要求的严格稳定性和安全性保障直接冲突。本综述对如何在不损害闭环保障的前提下将LLM引入NCS、CPS和CNS的控制回路进行了统一分析。我们围绕一个核心原则展开：LLM作为一个缓慢的监督者来调整高层目标和约束，而一个快速的、经过认证的内回路维持物理稳定性。在这一框架下，LLM的集成直接对应于经典的网络化控制挑战：推理延迟对应于时延，API故障对应于丢包，分词过程对应于量化，幻觉则对应于有界扰动。
tldr: 本综述提出一个分层控制框架，让大语言模型作为缓慢监督者调整高层目标与约束、由快速认证的内回路维持物理稳定性，从而将LLM的推理延迟、API故障、分词和幻觉分别映射为经典网络化控制中的时延、丢包、量化和有界扰动问题。
